issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as double, while the reference solution defines these attributes as int. Additionally, the UML lists getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning int — summing doubles but returning int is inconsistent and will confuse students about whether student counts should be integer or floating-point.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the types consistent across specification and implementation. Preferably change the UML in problem_statement.md to declare numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as int (counts are integral), so it matches the solution and the int return type of getTotalNumberOfStudents(). Alternatively, if fractional student counts are intentional, update the solution and UML return types so getTotalNumberOfStudents() and related methods use double consistently and adjust method signatures accordingly.
